S4. Likelihood judgments and evidence reinterpretation (RQ1)

October 10, 2026
Emma Marshall, J.D., M.A.
University of Nebraska-Lincoln

Likelihood judgments (H1a–H1g)

Table S4.1

Equivalence tests for H1b and H1g: two one-sided tests with the registered 90% interval

Comparison Estimate 90% CI Bounds p (lower) p (upper) Decision
Note. Two one-sided tests (TOST) of equivalence. Bounds = equivalence bounds [lower, upper] on the estimate's scale. Registered equivalence bounds: −5 to 5 points on the 0-100 likelihood scale. p (lower) tests the null that the difference is at or below the lower bound; p (upper), that it is at or above the upper bound. 90% CI = Student t confidence interval. Estimated with marginaleffects 0.32.0. The saved TOST p value (the larger of the two) equals the larger of the two one-sided p values shown. N = 320 (Stereotypical, None, n = 55; Stereotypical, SMA, n = 52; Stereotypical, NCM, n = 60; Non-stereotypical, None, n = 52; Non-stereotypical, SMA, n = 50; Non-stereotypical, NCM, n = 51).

Table S4.3

Every saved H1 comparison, all four sample and adjustment versions

Comparison ID Letter Estimate SE t df p Interval Omnibus test Protected p Tukey (check)
Note. Every comparison the analysis saves for the two ANCOVAs, in each of the four versions: the restricted-versus-full F, the within-evidence comparisons, the averaged comparisons (the stereotypicality-fallback secondary estimates), the baseline expectation and the between-evidence differences of each outcome effect. Adjusted versions control for the four attitude measures; unadjusted versions do not. Rows marked (reported), SMA − NCM within each evidence condition, are reported comparisons, not registered ones: the registration compares each outcome condition with no outcome information and treats every other comparison as exploratory, so they carry no letter, direction or decision. I added them after registration (2026-09-29), using the fitted models. Rows marked (reported) were added after registration and were tested with Fisher's protected least significant difference procedure; a comparison is significant only when the omnibus test of the three outcome conditions is significant (Levin et al., 1994). Omnibus test = the joint test that SMA − None and NCM − None within that evidence condition are both zero, F(2, residual df), from the same fit and coefficient covariance as the comparisons (not the restricted-versus-full F). Protected p = the larger of the comparison's own p and the omnibus p; a reported comparison is significant when its protected p is below .05. — = a saved row: the registration tests its comparisons without an omnibus gate. Tukey-adjusted p values are shown as a check on the procedure; the significance decisions follow the protected least significant difference procedure. Intervals: Student t with the residual df from the full coefficient covariance, 95% for every row except the two equivalence rows (H1b, H1g), which carry the registered 90% TOST interval. N = 320 (Stereotypical, None, n = 55; Stereotypical, SMA, n = 52; Stereotypical, NCM, n = 60; Non-stereotypical, None, n = 52; Non-stereotypical, SMA, n = 50; Non-stereotypical, NCM, n = 51). In the sensitivity analysis, N = 212 (Stereotypical, None, n = 32; Stereotypical, SMA, n = 33; Stereotypical, NCM, n = 45; Non-stereotypical, None, n = 36; Non-stereotypical, SMA, n = 29; Non-stereotypical, NCM, n = 37).

Table S4.4

Baseline expectations: stereotypical minus non-stereotypical evidence in the None condition

Version Expected Estimate SE t df p 95% CI
Note. Difference between the two no-information conditions (stereotypical minus non-stereotypical evidence), read from the separate no-information baselines of each H1 model.
